chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh and Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Hisham al-Mashriqi, that he entered upon Abi al-Hasan al-Khurasani (peace be upon him) and said:

The people of Basra asked about speech (kalam), saying: Yunus says that speech is not created. I said to them: Yunus has spoken the truth, speech is not created. Has the statement of Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him) not reached you when he was asked about the Qur'an: 'Is it creator or created?' He said to them: It is not creator nor created, rather it is the speech of the Creator. Thus the position of Yunus was strengthened. And they said: Yunus says that it is from the Sunnah for a man to pray two units while seated after the late night prayer? I said: Yunus has spoken the truth.

key_terms.الْكَلَام: Speech (specifically divine speech in theological context)

ai.seo_question: What is the theological status of the Qur'an as divine speech according to Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman?
ai.summary: This narration from Rijal al-Kashshi highlights Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman’s theological precision regarding the nature of divine speech (kalam), affirming it is neither created nor the Creator, a stance rooted in the Imam’s response to the Qur'an's ontological status. It further validates his juristic practice of performing two voluntary rak'ahs seated after the 'Isha prayer, reflecting the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding prayer postures in specific contexts.
